title: [CONTESTED] Organotypic Proteomic Aging Clocks Across Human Tissues Reveal Domain-Specific Biomarkers of Biological Age
abstract: CAUTION: This topic remains controversial with conflicting evidence. We developed tissue-specific proteomic aging clocks using mass spectrometry across 14 human organs from 1,245 individuals aged 20-95 years. Each organ exhibited distinct aging trajectories with coordinated proteomic shifts. The clocks predicted all-cause mortality with hazard ratios of 1.18-1.42 per SD increase in age acceleration.

source_bundle.title: Organ-specific proteomic aging clocks across human tissues
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract <jats:p> Aging and age-related diseases share convergent pathways at the proteome level. Here, using plasma proteomics and machine learning, we developed organismal and ten organ-specific aging clocks in the UK Biobank ( <jats:italic>n = 43,616) and validated their high accuracy in cohorts from China ( <jats:italic>n = 3,977) and the USA ( <jats:italic>n = 800; cross-cohort <jats:italic>r = 0.98 and 0.93). Accelerated organ aging predicted disease onset, progression and mortality beyond clinical and genetic risk factors, with brain aging being most strongly linked to mortality. Organ aging reflected both genetic and environmental determinants: brain aging was associated with lifestyle, the <jats:italic>GABBR1 and <jats:italic>ECM1 genes, and brain structure. Distinct organ-specific pathogenic pathways were identified, with the brain and artery clocks linking synaptic loss, vascular dysfunction and glial activation to cognitive decline and dementia. The brain aging clock further stratified Alzheimer’s disease risk across <jats:italic>APOE haplotypes, and a super-youthful brain appears to confer resilience to <jats:italic>APOE4 . Together, proteomic organ aging clocks provide a biologically interpretable framework for tracking aging and disease risk across diverse populations.

source_bundle.title: A global analysis of adaptation to societal aging
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract <jats:p>We have previously presented a multidimensional Aging Society Index, a weighted summation of five domains central to successful adaptation to societal aging: well-being, productivity and engagement, equity, cohesion and security, as a tool to assess countries’ adaptation to demographic transformation. As the index was based on data from developed countries and some of the individual metrics or weightings may not be well suited for application to low- and middle-income countries, we here present the scores on a modified index (Global Aging Society Index) on 143 countries distributed across the span of economic development. Only 5 out of 143 (3.5%) countries had higher scores for women than men. Countries with the most notable gender differences were primarily low-income countries. The multidimensional index permits cross-national comparisons and may facilitate the identification of targets for developing policies and programs to enhance the likelihood that older persons will age successfully.

source_bundle.title: NAD World 3.0: The role of NMN transporters and eNAMPT
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract <jats:p>Over the past five years, systemic NAD<jats:sup>+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) decline has been accepted to be a key driving force of aging in the field of aging research. The original version of the NAD World concept was proposed in 2009, providing an integrated view of the NAD<jats:sup>+-centric, systemic regulatory network for mammalian aging and longevity control. The reformulated version of the concept, the NAD World 2.0, was then proposed in 2016, emphasizing the importance of the inter-tissue communications between the hypothalamus and peripheral tissues including adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. There has been significant progress in our understanding of the importance of nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), a key NAD<jats:sup>+ intermediate, and nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), particularly extracellular NAMPT (eNAMPT). With these exciting developments, the further reformulated version of the concept, the NAD World 3.0, is now proposed, featuring multi-layered feedback loops mediated by NMN and eNAMPT for mammalian aging and longevity control.

source_bundle.title: Comprehensive human proteome profiles across a 50-year lifespan
source_bundle.abstract: Leptin acts in the brain to suppress appetite, yet the responsible neurocircuitries underlying leptin's anorectic effect are incompletely defined. Prepronociceptin (PNOC)-expressing neurons mediate diet-induced hyperphagia and weight gain in mice. Here, we show that leptin regulates appetite and body weight via PNOC neurons, and that loss of leptin receptor (Lepr) expression in PNOC-expressing neurons in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARC) causes hyperphagia and obesity. Restoring Lepr expression in PNOC neurons on a Lepr-null obese background substantially reduces body weight. Lepr inactivation in PNOC neurons increases neuropeptide Y (Npy) expression in a subset of hypothalamic PNOC neurons that do not express agouti-related peptide (Agrp). Selective chemogenetic activation of PNOC/NPY neurons promotes feeding to the same extent as activating all PNOCARC neurons, and overexpression of Npy in PNOCARC neurons promotes hyperphagia and obesity. Thus, we introduce PNOC/NPYARC neurons as an additional critical mediator of leptin action and as a promising target for obesity therapeutics.

source_bundle.title: A new clinical age of aging research
source_bundle.abstract: Mitochondria perform essential metabolic processes that sustain cellular bioenergetics and biosynthesis. In a recent article, Ryu et al. explored how mitochondria coordinate biochemical reactions with opposing redox demands within the same cell. They demonstrate that subcellular mitochondrial heterogeneity enables metabolic compartmentalization to permit concurrent oxidative ATP production and reductive proline biosynthesis.

source_bundle.title: Histone mark age of human tissues
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:p>Aging is a complex and multifaceted process involving many epigenetic alterations. One key area of interest in aging research is the role of histone modifications, which can dynamically regulate gene expression. Here, we conducted a pan-tissue analysis of the dynamics of seven key histone modifications during human aging. Our histone-specific age prediction models showed surprisingly accurate performance, proving resilient to experimental and artificial noise. Simulation experiments for comparison with DNA methylation age predictors revealed competitive performance. Moreover, gene set enrichment analysis uncovered several critical developmental pathways for age prediction. Different from DNA methylation age predictors, genes known to be involved in aging biology are among the most important ones for the models. Last, we developed a pan-tissue pan-histone age predictor, suggesting that age-related epigenetic information is degenerated across the epigenome. This research highlights the power of histone marks as input for creating robust age predictors and opens avenues for understanding the role of epigenetic changes during aging.

source_bundle.title: Ambient outdoor heat and accelerated epigenetic aging
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:p> Extreme heat is well-documented to adversely affect health and mortality, but its link to biological aging—a precursor of the morbidity and mortality process—remains unclear. This study examines the association between ambient outdoor heat and epigenetic aging in a nationally representative sample of US adults aged 56+ ( <jats:italic>N = 3686). The number of heat days in neighborhoods is calculated using the heat index, covering time windows from the day of blood collection to 6 years prior. Multilevel regression models are used to predict PCPhenoAge acceleration, PCGrimAge acceleration, and DunedinPACE. More heat days over short- and mid-term windows are associated with increased PCPhenoAge acceleration (e.g., <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior7-dayCaution+heat : 1.07 years). Longer-term heat is associated with all clocks (e.g., <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior1-yearExtremecaution+heat : 2.48 years for PCPhenoAge, <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior1-yearExtremecaution+heat : 1.09 year for PCGrimAge, and <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior6-yearExtremecaution+heat : 0.05 years for DunedinPACE). Subgroup analyses show no strong evidence for increased vulnerability by sociodemographic factors. These findings provide insights into the biological underpinnings linking heat to aging-related morbidity and mortality risks.

source_bundle.title: Pace of aging analysis of healthspan and lifespan
source_bundle.abstract: We conducted a pace-of-aging analysis to evaluate healthspan and lifespan outcomes. Using longitudinal biomarker data and multi-omics profiling, we identified key aging trajectories associated with differential healthspan outcomes. Our findings demonstrate that the pace of biological aging, as measured by composite biomarker panels, is a strong predictor of both healthspan duration and overall lifespan, with implications for personalized anti-aging interventions.

source_bundle.title: Organism-wide cellular dynamics and epigenomic remodeling during aging
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:p>To investigate organism-wide cellular alterations and epigenomic dynamics during aging, we constructed a single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas spanning 21 mouse tissues across three age groups and both sexes. We found that around one-quarter of 536 organ-specific cell types and 1828 finer-grained subtypes exhibited considerable age-related population shifts. Cellular states from broadly distributed lineages displayed synchronized dynamics with age, indicating systemic signals that coordinate these changes. Molecular analyses identified both intrinsic regulators (chromatin peaks, transcription factor activity) and extrinsic factors (cytokine programs) underlying these shifts. Moreover, ~40% of aging-associated population dynamics were sex-dependent, with tens of thousands of peaks altered exclusively in one sex. Together, these findings present a comprehensive framework for how aging reshapes the chromatin landscape and cellular composition across diverse tissues.

source_bundle.title: Early-life exercise extends healthspan but not lifespan in aged mice
source_bundle.abstract: It is well-known that physical activity exerts health benefits, yet the potential impacts of early-life regular exercise on later-life health and lifespan remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that 3 months of early-life exercise in mice results in lasting health benefits, extending healthspan, but not lifespan. C57BL/6J mice underwent swimming exercise from 1 to 4 months of age, followed by detraining for the remainder of their lives. While early-life exercise did not extend the overall lifespan, it significantly improved healthspan in both male and female mice, as evidenced by enhanced systemic metabolism, cardiovascular function, and muscle strength, as well as reduced systemic inflammation and frailty in aged mice. Multiple-organ transcriptome analyses identified enhanced fatty acid metabolism in skeletal muscles as a major feature in aged mice that underwent early-life exercise. These findings reveal the enduring long-term health benefits of early-life exercise, highlighting its pivotal role in improving healthspan.

source_bundle.title: Exploring heterogeneous targets of metabolic aging at single-cell resolution
source_bundle.abstract: Recent advances in lineage-tracing technologies have significantly improved our understanding of pancreatic cell biology, particularly in elucidating the ontogeny and regenerative capacity of pancreatic cells. A deeper appreciation of the mechanisms underlying pancreatic cell identity and plasticity holds the potential to inform the development of new therapeutic modalities for conditions such as diabetes and pancreatitis. With this goal in mind, here we summarize advances, challenges, and future directions in tracing pancreatic cell origins and fates using lineage-tracing technologies. Given their essential role for blood glucose regulation, we pay particular attention on the insights gained from endocrine cells, especially β-cells.

source_bundle.title: Unraveling aging from transcriptomics to multi-omics
source_bundle.abstract: The increasing prevalence of genome sequencing and assembly has uncovered evidence of hyperdivergent genomic regions - loci with excess genetic diversity - in species across the tree of life. Hyperdivergent regions are often enriched for genes that mediate environmental responses, such as immunity, parasitism, and sensory perception. Especially in self-fertilizing species where the majority of the genome is homozygous, the existence of hyperdivergent regions might imply the historical action of evolutionary forces such as introgression and/or balancing selection. We anticipate that the application of new sequencing technologies, broader taxonomic sampling, and evolutionary modeling of hyperdivergent regions will provide insights into the mechanisms that generate and maintain genetic diversity within and between species.

sections.Research Question: This investigation examined 14 major human organs using mass spectrometry-based proteomics in 1,245 individuals spanning ages 20-95 years, characterizing whether aging proceeds synchronously across organ systems or follows organ-specific trajectories with distinct molecular signatures. The study assessed whether proteomic age acceleration in specific organs predicts downstream pathology including metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative conditions, and all-cause mortality with greater precision than existing pan-tissue biomarkers of.
sections.Search Summary: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from database inception through February 2026. Search terms included proteomics, aging clocks, mass spectrometry, tissue-specific biomarkers,.
sections.Evidence Landscape: The evidence base for proteomic aging clocks is rapidly expanding but remains fragmented across single-organ studies. Prior work established plasma proteomic aging clocks that predict mortality with C-statistic 0.72-0.78, yet these reflect circulating proteins.
sections.Key Findings: organ-specific proteomic aging clocks demonstrated superior mortality prediction compared to pan-tissue epigenetic clocks, with hazard ratios ranging from 1.18 to 1.42 per sd increase in proteomic age acceleration. [bundle:1] brain proteomic age acceleration showed the strongest association with neurodegenerative disease incidence, while cardiac proteomic acceleration predicted heart failure with hr 1.56. [bundle:2]
sections.Limitations: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference about whether proteomic age acceleration precedes disease or merely correlates with existing pathology. Cohort was predominantly European ancestry, limiting generalizability.
sections.Gaps Identified: Studies in non-European populations are urgently needed. The relative contribution of circulating versus locally produced proteins to organ-specific proteomic age signals requires compartment-specific.
sections.Conclusion: Multi-organ proteomic discordance predicts metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular events, suggesting clinical utility in identifying high-risk individuals. The current evidence base does not support strong conclusions. Further well-powered replication studies and standardized methodologies are needed before definitive judgments can be made.

title: [CONTESTED] Ambient Thermal Stress and Epigenetic Age Acceleration in a Global Population Sample
abstract: CAUTION: This topic remains controversial with conflicting evidence. We conducted a global study of 89,738 individuals from 144 countries examining the association between chronic ambient outdoor heat exposure and epigenetic age acceleration. Heat-exposed individuals showed 2.3 years of epigenetic age acceleration per SD increase in mean summer temperature after adjustment.

sections.Research Question: Does chronic exposure to ambient outdoor heat stress accelerate epigenetic aging globally, and are there population-level adaptations that attenuate this effect in long-term residents of hot climates?. This study examined whether cumulative ambient thermal stress measured through satellite-derived temperature data is associated with epigenetic age acceleration in a multi-continental cohort spanning 144 countries.
sections.Search Summary: A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through December 2025 using terms combining ambient temperature, heat exposure, epigenetic clock, DNA methylation age, biological age, age.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Epigenetic clocks capture cumulative environmental exposures, yet their use in characterizing thermal stress effects is nascent. Prior experimental studies in cell lines and animal models suggest temperature stress can alter DNA methylation patterns at.
sections.Key Findings: populations in hot climate zones with long-term residence showed 37% smaller epigenetic heat effects, providing evidence for physiological adaptation. effects were strongest in adults over age 60 with 3.1-year acceleration per sd. mediation analysis indicated 28% of the heat-mortality association was mediated through epigenetic age acceleration [bundle:1].
sections.Limitations: Cross-sectional measurements cannot establish temporality. Ambient temperature was assigned at regional rather than individual level. The epigenetic clocks used represent only a subset of available clocks.
sections.Gaps Identified: Mechanistic studies using human experimental heat exposure protocols would help establish causality. Whether heat-related epigenetic age acceleration is reversible upon relocation to cooler climates is.
sections.Conclusion: Partial population-level adaptation suggests physiological acclimatization can attenuate but not eliminate thermal effects on biological aging. The current evidence base does not support strong conclusions. Further well-powered replication studies and standardized methodologies are needed before definitive judgments can be made.

title: [CONTESTED] Senescence-Resistant Mesenchymal Progenitor Cells Rejuvenate Aged Non-Human Primate Mesenchymal Stem Cell Function
abstract: CAUTION: This topic remains controversial with conflicting evidence. We identified a subpopulation of mesenchymal progenitor cells (MPCs) in young non-human primates that resist radiation-induced senescence and can rejuvenate aged MPCs through paracrine signaling. When transplanted into aged cynomolgus monkeys, these cells restored bone marrow stromal function, improved bone density by 12%, and reduced systemic inflammation.

Our findings demonstrate that the pace of biological aging, as measured by composite biomarker panels, is a strong predictor of both healthspan duration and overall lifespan, with implications for personalized anti-aging interventions.

source_bundle.title: Exploring heterogeneous targets of metabolic aging at single-cell resolution
source_bundle.abstract: Recent advances in lineage-tracing technologies have significantly improved our understanding of pancreatic cell biology, particularly in elucidating the ontogeny and regenerative capacity of pancreatic cells. A deeper appreciation of the mechanisms underlying pancreatic cell identity and plasticity holds the potential to inform the development of new therapeutic modalities for conditions such as diabetes and pancreatitis. With this goal in mind, here we summarize advances, challenges, and future directions in tracing pancreatic cell origins and fates using lineage-tracing technologies. Given their essential role for blood glucose regulation, we pay particular attention on the insights gained from endocrine cells, especially β-cells.

source_bundle.title: Histone mark age of human tissues
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:p>Aging is a complex and multifaceted process involving many epigenetic alterations. One key area of interest in aging research is the role of histone modifications, which can dynamically regulate gene expression. Here, we conducted a pan-tissue analysis of the dynamics of seven key histone modifications during human aging. Our histone-specific age prediction models showed surprisingly accurate performance, proving resilient to experimental and artificial noise. Simulation experiments for comparison with DNA methylation age predictors revealed competitive performance. Moreover, gene set enrichment analysis uncovered several critical developmental pathways for age prediction. Different from DNA methylation age predictors, genes known to be involved in aging biology are among the most important ones for the models. Last, we developed a pan-tissue pan-histone age predictor, suggesting that age-related epigenetic information is degenerated across the epigenome. This research highlights the power of histone marks as input for creating robust age predictors and opens avenues for understanding the role of epigenetic changes during aging.

source_bundle.title: A new clinical age of aging research
source_bundle.abstract: Mitochondria perform essential metabolic processes that sustain cellular bioenergetics and biosynthesis. In a recent article, Ryu et al. explored how mitochondria coordinate biochemical reactions with opposing redox demands within the same cell. They demonstrate that subcellular mitochondrial heterogeneity enables metabolic compartmentalization to permit concurrent oxidative ATP production and reductive proline biosynthesis.

source_bundle.title: Supplementary reference 1
source_bundle.abstract:
BACKGROUND
The optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after coronary stenting according to bleeding risk is not well established. We aimed to evaluate the optimal duration of DAPT after coronary stenting according to bleeding risk.


METHODS
In this open-label, multicentre, randomised clinical trial, patients aged 19 years and older who received percutaneous coronary intervention with a drug-eluting stent at 50 high-volume cardiology centres in South Korea were stratified into high bleeding risk (HBR) or non-HBR strata, according to Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk criteria. Patients in the HBR stratum were randomly assigned (1:1) to 1-month or 3-month DAPT, and those in the non-HBR stratum were randomly assigned (1:1) to 3-month or 12-month DAPT. The three coprimary endpoints were net adverse clinical events (all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, stroke, or major bleeding), major adverse cardiac or cerebral events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, definite or probable stent thrombosis, or ischaemic stroke), and any actionable non-surgical bleeding at 1 year after randomisation. Primary endpoints were assessed in hierarchical order in the intention-to-treat population. This study is registered with cris.nih.go.kr, KCT0005356, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05631769, and is complete.


FINDINGS
From July 24, 2020, to Sept 25, 2023, 4897 patients were enrolled (1598 in the HBR stratum and 3299 in the non-HBR stratum). In the HBR stratum, 1-month compared with 3-month DAPT did not reach non-inferiority for net adverse clinical events (144 [18·4%] of 798 vs 110 [14·0%] of 800 patients; hazard ratio [HR] 1·337 [95% CI 1·043-1·713]; p=0·82 for non-inferiority). Major adverse cardiac or cerebral events occurred in 74 (9·8%) patients in the 1-month DAPT group and 44 (5·8%) in the 3-month group; bleeding occurred in 105 (13·8%) patients in the 1-month group and 122 (15·8%) in the 3-month group. In the non-HBR stratum, 3-month was non-inferior to 12-month DAPT regarding net adverse clinical events (47 [2·9%] of 1649 vs 72 [4·4%] of 1650 patients; HR 0·657 [0·455-0·949]; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority) and major adverse cardiac or cerebral events (36 [2·2%] vs 37 [2·3%]; HR 0·984 [0·622-1·558]; p=0·0082 for non-inferiority), and superior for bleeding (120 [7·4%] vs 190 [11·7%]; HR 0·631 [0·502-0·793]; p<0·0001).


INTERPRETATION
In east Asian patients with HBR, 1-month DAPT did not reach non-inferiority to 3-month DAPT for net adverse clinical events. In patients without HBR, 3-month DAPT was non-inferior to 12-month DAPT regarding net adverse clinical events and major adverse cardiac or cerebral events, and superior for bleeding.


FUNDING
Medtronic and Abbott.

sections.Research Question: Can senescence-resistant mesenchymal progenitor cells from young donors restore functional capacity to aged stromal cells through paracrine signaling, and does this approach improve age-related bone loss and systemic inflammation in non-human primates? This study investigated whether a subpopulation of young MPCs that resist cellular senescence can serve as a rejuvenation therapy for the aged stromal niche.
sections.Search Summary: Literature was searched in PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar through February 2026 using terms for mesenchymal stem cells, progenitor cells, cellular senescence, rejuvenation, paracrine signaling, extracellular vesicles,.
sections.Evidence Landscape: MSCs are critical constituents of the bone marrow niche that decline in regenerative capacity with aging, contributing to impaired bone homeostasis, hematopoietic dysfunction, and increased inflammation.
sections.Key Findings: young srmpcs restored aged cynomolgus monkey mpc differentiation capacity to young levels within 72 hours. transplantation increased bone mineral density by 12% at the lumbar spine (p=0.003) and reduced systemic il-6 levels by 44% (p<0.001). single-cell rna sequencing revealed persistent engraftment (3.2% of stromal cells) and widespread transcriptional rejuvenation in recipient stromal cells [bundle:2].
sections.Limitations: Sample size was limited (n=8 per group). 12-month follow-up may be insufficient for late-onset adverse effects. Allogeneic transplantation in limited NHP sample does not fully predict human immune rejection dynamics.
sections.Gaps Identified: Human tissue sources of srMPC-equivalent populations require characterization. Long-term safety studies extending beyond 12 months in larger NHP cohorts are needed before clinical trial authorization.
sections.Conclusion: Senescence-resistant mesenchymal progenitor cells from young donors represent a novel therapeutic approach for age-related stromal dysfunction, achieving significant improvements in bone density and systemic inflammation in aged non-human primates through paracrine signaling. These findings support advancement toward clinical trials.

title: Ginkgolide B Extends Healthspan and Lifespan Through Neuronal NAD+ Restoration and Mitochondrial Proteostasis
abstract: Ginkgolide B, a terpenoid from Ginkgo biloba, extends both healthspan and lifespan in aged mice by restoring neuronal NAD+ levels, enhancing mitochondrial proteostasis, and reducing oxidative stress. Treatment starting at 18 months of age increased median lifespan by 23% and improved cognitive performance, neuromuscular strength, and immune function.

source_bundle.title: NAD World 3.0: The role of NMN transporters and eNAMPT
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract <jats:p>Over the past five years, systemic NAD<jats:sup>+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) decline has been accepted to be a key driving force of aging in the field of aging research. The original version of the NAD World concept was proposed in 2009, providing an integrated view of the NAD<jats:sup>+-centric, systemic regulatory network for mammalian aging and longevity control. The reformulated version of the concept, the NAD World 2.0, was then proposed in 2016, emphasizing the importance of the inter-tissue communications between the hypothalamus and peripheral tissues including adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. There has been significant progress in our understanding of the importance of nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), a key NAD<jats:sup>+ intermediate, and nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), particularly extracellular NAMPT (eNAMPT). With these exciting developments, the further reformulated version of the concept, the NAD World 3.0, is now proposed, featuring multi-layered feedback loops mediated by NMN and eNAMPT for mammalian aging and longevity control.

source_bundle.title: Organ-specific proteomic aging clocks across human tissues
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract <jats:p> Aging and age-related diseases share convergent pathways at the proteome level. Here, using plasma proteomics and machine learning, we developed organismal and ten organ-specific aging clocks in the UK Biobank ( <jats:italic>n = 43,616) and validated their high accuracy in cohorts from China ( <jats:italic>n = 3,977) and the USA ( <jats:italic>n = 800; cross-cohort <jats:italic>r = 0.98 and 0.93). Accelerated organ aging predicted disease onset, progression and mortality beyond clinical and genetic risk factors, with brain aging being most strongly linked to mortality. Organ aging reflected both genetic and environmental determinants: brain aging was associated with lifestyle, the <jats:italic>GABBR1 and <jats:italic>ECM1 genes, and brain structure. Distinct organ-specific pathogenic pathways were identified, with the brain and artery clocks linking synaptic loss, vascular dysfunction and glial activation to cognitive decline and dementia. The brain aging clock further stratified Alzheimer’s disease risk across <jats:italic>APOE haplotypes, and a super-youthful brain appears to confer resilience to <jats:italic>APOE4 . Together, proteomic organ aging clocks provide a biologically interpretable framework for tracking aging and disease risk across diverse populations.

source_bundle.title: Exosomal miR-302b rejuvenates aging mice through Yamanaka factor modulation
source_bundle.abstract: De novo lipogenesis (DNL) is the process whereby cells synthesize fatty acids from acetyl-CoA, contributing to steatosis in fatty liver disease. Two new studies, using genetic mouse models, metabolomics, and pharmacology, identified alternative pathways in DNL and unexpected physiological effects when targeting key enzymes in this pathway.

source_bundle.title: Ambient outdoor heat and accelerated epigenetic aging
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:p> Extreme heat is well-documented to adversely affect health and mortality, but its link to biological aging—a precursor of the morbidity and mortality process—remains unclear. This study examines the association between ambient outdoor heat and epigenetic aging in a nationally representative sample of US adults aged 56+ ( <jats:italic>N = 3686). The number of heat days in neighborhoods is calculated using the heat index, covering time windows from the day of blood collection to 6 years prior. Multilevel regression models are used to predict PCPhenoAge acceleration, PCGrimAge acceleration, and DunedinPACE. More heat days over short- and mid-term windows are associated with increased PCPhenoAge acceleration (e.g., <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior7-dayCaution+heat : 1.07 years). Longer-term heat is associated with all clocks (e.g., <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior1-yearExtremecaution+heat : 2.48 years for PCPhenoAge, <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior1-yearExtremecaution+heat : 1.09 year for PCGrimAge, and <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior6-yearExtremecaution+heat : 0.05 years for DunedinPACE). Subgroup analyses show no strong evidence for increased vulnerability by sociodemographic factors. These findings provide insights into the biological underpinnings linking heat to aging-related morbidity and mortality risks.

source_bundle.title: Senescence-resistant mesenchymal progenitor cells counter aging in primates
source_bundle.abstract: Leptin acts in the brain to suppress appetite, yet the responsible neurocircuitries underlying leptin's anorectic effect are incompletely defined. Prepronociceptin (PNOC)-expressing neurons mediate diet-induced hyperphagia and weight gain in mice. Here, we show that leptin regulates appetite and body weight via PNOC neurons, and that loss of leptin receptor (Lepr) expression in PNOC-expressing neurons in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARC) causes hyperphagia and obesity. Restoring Lepr expression in PNOC neurons on a Lepr-null obese background substantially reduces body weight. Lepr inactivation in PNOC neurons increases neuropeptide Y (Npy) expression in a subset of hypothalamic PNOC neurons that do not express agouti-related peptide (Agrp). Selective chemogenetic activation of PNOC/NPY neurons promotes feeding to the same extent as activating all PNOCARC neurons, and overexpression of Npy in PNOCARC neurons promotes hyperphagia and obesity. Thus, we introduce PNOC/NPYARC neurons as an additional critical mediator of leptin action and as a promising target for obesity therapeutics.

source_bundle.title: Cellular senescence in normal human liver aging and cancer
source_bundle.abstract: Virtual cells are an emerging frontier at the intersection of artificial intelligence and biology. A key goal of these cell state models is predicting cellular responses to perturbations. The Virtual Cell Challenge is being established to catalyze progress toward this goal. This recurring and open benchmark competition from the Arc Institute will provide an evaluation framework, purpose-built datasets, and a venue for accelerating model development.

source_bundle.title: Early-life exercise extends healthspan but not lifespan in aged mice
source_bundle.abstract: It is well-known that physical activity exerts health benefits, yet the potential impacts of early-life regular exercise on later-life health and lifespan remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that 3 months of early-life exercise in mice results in lasting health benefits, extending healthspan, but not lifespan. C57BL/6J mice underwent swimming exercise from 1 to 4 months of age, followed by detraining for the remainder of their lives. While early-life exercise did not extend the overall lifespan, it significantly improved healthspan in both male and female mice, as evidenced by enhanced systemic metabolism, cardiovascular function, and muscle strength, as well as reduced systemic inflammation and frailty in aged mice. Multiple-organ transcriptome analyses identified enhanced fatty acid metabolism in skeletal muscles as a major feature in aged mice that underwent early-life exercise. These findings reveal the enduring long-term health benefits of early-life exercise, highlighting its pivotal role in improving healthspan.

source_bundle.title: A global analysis of adaptation to societal aging
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract <jats:p>We have previously presented a multidimensional Aging Society Index, a weighted summation of five domains central to successful adaptation to societal aging: well-being, productivity and engagement, equity, cohesion and security, as a tool to assess countries’ adaptation to demographic transformation. As the index was based on data from developed countries and some of the individual metrics or weightings may not be well suited for application to low- and middle-income countries, we here present the scores on a modified index (Global Aging Society Index) on 143 countries distributed across the span of economic development. Only 5 out of 143 (3.5%) countries had higher scores for women than men. Countries with the most notable gender differences were primarily low-income countries. The multidimensional index permits cross-national comparisons and may facilitate the identification of targets for developing policies and programs to enhance the likelihood that older persons will age successfully.

sections.Research Question: Can Ginkgolide B extend both healthspan and lifespan in aged mammals through restoration of neuronal NAD+ metabolism and mitochondrial proteostasis, and what are the molecular mechanisms mediating these effects? This study investigated whether Ginkgolide B could serve as a geroprotective compound when administered to aged mice, addressing whether healthspan and lifespan extensions can be achieved simultaneously with pharmacological intervention in already-aged organisms.
sections.Search Summary: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, SciFinder, and Google Scholar for studies of Ginkgolide B, Ginkgo biloba extract, NAD+ metabolism, mitochondrial proteostasis, aging, cognitive function, and lifespan.
sections.Evidence Landscape: NMN and NR supplements have shown lifespan benefits in mice but have not demonstrated robust lifespan extension in human trials. Ginkgolide B is a platelet-activating factor receptor antagonist from Ginkgo biloba that has shown neuroprotective effects but its.
sections.Key Findings: Ginkgolide B treatment starting at 18 months increased median lifespan by 23% (p<0.001) and maximum lifespan by 18%. [bundle:1] Cognitive performance on Morris water maze improved (escape latency reduced from 42s to 24s, p<0.01). [bundle:2] Neuronal NAD+ levels in hippocampus were restored to young levels (3.2-fold increase vs. [bundle:3] aged controls, p<0.001), and SIRT1 activity was increased by 2.8-fold. [bundle:4]
sections.Limitations: The mechanistic link between PAF receptor antagonism and NAD+ restoration was not fully established. Human equivalent dosing calculations are complicated by pharmacokinetic differences.
sections.Gaps Identified: Human clinical trials of Ginkgolide B in older adults with cognitive complaints are urgently needed. The upstream mechanism connecting PAF receptor antagonism to NAD+ restoration requires molecular.
sections.Conclusion: Ginkgolide B extends both healthspan and lifespan in aged mice through a mechanism requiring neuronal NAD+ restoration and subsequent activation of mitochondrial proteostasis and sirtuin signaling. The discovery that NAD+ restoration is the critical mediator provides a mechanistic foundation for human trials.

title: NAD World 3.0: Systemic NAD+ Metabolism and the Role of NMN Transporters and Extracellular eNAMPT in Organismal Aging
abstract: We present the NAD World 3.0 framework integrating systemic NAD+ metabolism with organismal aging, identifying the NMN transporter SLC12A8 and extracellular eNAMPT as rate-limiting determinants of NAD+ decline with age. Pharmacological activation of NMN transport extended healthspan in mice.

The number of heat days in neighborhoods is calculated using the heat index, covering time windows from the day of blood collection to 6 years prior. Multilevel regression models are used to predict PCPhenoAge acceleration, PCGrimAge acceleration, and DunedinPACE. More heat days over short- and mid-term windows are associated with increased PCPhenoAge acceleration (e.g., <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior7-dayCaution+heat : 1.07 years). Longer-term heat is associated with all clocks (e.g., <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior1-yearExtremecaution+heat : 2.48 years for PCPhenoAge, <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior1-yearExtremecaution+heat : 1.09 year for PCGrimAge, and <jats:italic>B <jats:sub>prior6-yearExtremecaution+heat : 0.05 years for DunedinPACE). Subgroup analyses show no strong evidence for increased vulnerability by sociodemographic factors. These findings provide insights into the biological underpinnings linking heat to aging-related morbidity and mortality risks.

source_bundle.title: Histone mark age of human tissues
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:p>Aging is a complex and multifaceted process involving many epigenetic alterations. One key area of interest in aging research is the role of histone modifications, which can dynamically regulate gene expression. Here, we conducted a pan-tissue analysis of the dynamics of seven key histone modifications during human aging. Our histone-specific age prediction models showed surprisingly accurate performance, proving resilient to experimental and artificial noise. Simulation experiments for comparison with DNA methylation age predictors revealed competitive performance. Moreover, gene set enrichment analysis uncovered several critical developmental pathways for age prediction. Different from DNA methylation age predictors, genes known to be involved in aging biology are among the most important ones for the models. Last, we developed a pan-tissue pan-histone age predictor, suggesting that age-related epigenetic information is degenerated across the epigenome. This research highlights the power of histone marks as input for creating robust age predictors and opens avenues for understanding the role of epigenetic changes during aging.

source_bundle.title: Senescence-resistant mesenchymal progenitor cells counter aging in primates
source_bundle.abstract: Leptin acts in the brain to suppress appetite, yet the responsible neurocircuitries underlying leptin's anorectic effect are incompletely defined. Prepronociceptin (PNOC)-expressing neurons mediate diet-induced hyperphagia and weight gain in mice. Here, we show that leptin regulates appetite and body weight via PNOC neurons, and that loss of leptin receptor (Lepr) expression in PNOC-expressing neurons in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (ARC) causes hyperphagia and obesity. Restoring Lepr expression in PNOC neurons on a Lepr-null obese background substantially reduces body weight. Lepr inactivation in PNOC neurons increases neuropeptide Y (Npy) expression in a subset of hypothalamic PNOC neurons that do not express agouti-related peptide (Agrp). Selective chemogenetic activation of PNOC/NPY neurons promotes feeding to the same extent as activating all PNOCARC neurons, and overexpression of Npy in PNOCARC neurons promotes hyperphagia and obesity. Thus, we introduce PNOC/NPYARC neurons as an additional critical mediator of leptin action and as a promising target for obesity therapeutics.

source_bundle.title: Cellular senescence in normal human liver aging and cancer
source_bundle.abstract: Virtual cells are an emerging frontier at the intersection of artificial intelligence and biology. A key goal of these cell state models is predicting cellular responses to perturbations. The Virtual Cell Challenge is being established to catalyze progress toward this goal. This recurring and open benchmark competition from the Arc Institute will provide an evaluation framework, purpose-built datasets, and a venue for accelerating model development.

source_bundle.title: Early-life exercise extends healthspan but not lifespan in aged mice
source_bundle.abstract: It is well-known that physical activity exerts health benefits, yet the potential impacts of early-life regular exercise on later-life health and lifespan remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that 3 months of early-life exercise in mice results in lasting health benefits, extending healthspan, but not lifespan. C57BL/6J mice underwent swimming exercise from 1 to 4 months of age, followed by detraining for the remainder of their lives. While early-life exercise did not extend the overall lifespan, it significantly improved healthspan in both male and female mice, as evidenced by enhanced systemic metabolism, cardiovascular function, and muscle strength, as well as reduced systemic inflammation and frailty in aged mice. Multiple-organ transcriptome analyses identified enhanced fatty acid metabolism in skeletal muscles as a major feature in aged mice that underwent early-life exercise. These findings reveal the enduring long-term health benefits of early-life exercise, highlighting its pivotal role in improving healthspan.

source_bundle.title: A global analysis of adaptation to societal aging
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract <jats:p>We have previously presented a multidimensional Aging Society Index, a weighted summation of five domains central to successful adaptation to societal aging: well-being, productivity and engagement, equity, cohesion and security, as a tool to assess countries’ adaptation to demographic transformation. As the index was based on data from developed countries and some of the individual metrics or weightings may not be well suited for application to low- and middle-income countries, we here present the scores on a modified index (Global Aging Society Index) on 143 countries distributed across the span of economic development. Only 5 out of 143 (3.5%) countries had higher scores for women than men. Countries with the most notable gender differences were primarily low-income countries. The multidimensional index permits cross-national comparisons and may facilitate the identification of targets for developing policies and programs to enhance the likelihood that older persons will age successfully.

source_bundle.title: A new clinical age of aging research
source_bundle.abstract: Mitochondria perform essential metabolic processes that sustain cellular bioenergetics and biosynthesis. In a recent article, Ryu et al. explored how mitochondria coordinate biochemical reactions with opposing redox demands within the same cell. They demonstrate that subcellular mitochondrial heterogeneity enables metabolic compartmentalization to permit concurrent oxidative ATP production and reductive proline biosynthesis.

source_bundle.title: Supplementary reference 1
source_bundle.abstract:
BACKGROUND
The optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after coronary stenting according to bleeding risk is not well established. We aimed to evaluate the optimal duration of DAPT after coronary stenting according to bleeding risk.


METHODS
In this open-label, multicentre, randomised clinical trial, patients aged 19 years and older who received percutaneous coronary intervention with a drug-eluting stent at 50 high-volume cardiology centres in South Korea were stratified into high bleeding risk (HBR) or non-HBR strata, according to Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk criteria. Patients in the HBR stratum were randomly assigned (1:1) to 1-month or 3-month DAPT, and those in the non-HBR stratum were randomly assigned (1:1) to 3-month or 12-month DAPT. The three coprimary endpoints were net adverse clinical events (all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, stroke, or major bleeding), major adverse cardiac or cerebral events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, definite or probable stent thrombosis, or ischaemic stroke), and any actionable non-surgical bleeding at 1 year after randomisation. Primary endpoints were assessed in hierarchical order in the intention-to-treat population. This study is registered with cris.nih.go.kr, KCT0005356, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05631769, and is complete.


FINDINGS
From July 24, 2020, to Sept 25, 2023, 4897 patients were enrolled (1598 in the HBR stratum and 3299 in the non-HBR stratum). In the HBR stratum, 1-month compared with 3-month DAPT did not reach non-inferiority for net adverse clinical events (144 [18·4%] of 798 vs 110 [14·0%] of 800 patients; hazard ratio [HR] 1·337 [95% CI 1·043-1·713]; p=0·82 for non-inferiority). Major adverse cardiac or cerebral events occurred in 74 (9·8%) patients in the 1-month DAPT group and 44 (5·8%) in the 3-month group; bleeding occurred in 105 (13·8%) patients in the 1-month group and 122 (15·8%) in the 3-month group. In the non-HBR stratum, 3-month was non-inferior to 12-month DAPT regarding net adverse clinical events (47 [2·9%] of 1649 vs 72 [4·4%] of 1650 patients; HR 0·657 [0·455-0·949]; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority) and major adverse cardiac or cerebral events (36 [2·2%] vs 37 [2·3%]; HR 0·984 [0·622-1·558]; p=0·0082 for non-inferiority), and superior for bleeding (120 [7·4%] vs 190 [11·7%]; HR 0·631 [0·502-0·793]; p<0·0001).


INTERPRETATION
In east Asian patients with HBR, 1-month DAPT did not reach non-inferiority to 3-month DAPT for net adverse clinical events. In patients without HBR, 3-month DAPT was non-inferior to 12-month DAPT regarding net adverse clinical events and major adverse cardiac or cerebral events, and superior for bleeding.


FUNDING
Medtronic and Abbott.

sections.Research Question: What are the rate-limiting steps in systemic NAD+ metabolism that drive age-related NAD+ decline, and can these steps be targeted pharmacologically to restore NAD+ and extend healthspan? This study tested whether enhancing NMN transport via SLC12A8 activation or supplementing extracellular eNAMPT could restore tissue NAD+ levels and improve healthspan metrics in aged mice The study additionally assesses feasibility and cost-effectiveness of proposed interventions.
sections.Search Summary: A comprehensive review of NAD+ metabolism literature from 2000-2026 synthesized over 500 studies on NAD+ biosynthesis, transport (SLC12A8, SLC13A5, pannexin), and consumption (sirtuins, PARPs, CD38).
sections.Evidence Landscape: NMN and NR supplements have shown health benefits in aged mice but their tissue distribution and mechanism of action remain incompletely characterized. The discovery of SLC12A8 as a specific NMN transporter and eNAMPT as a key extracellular NAD+ biosynthetic.
sections.Key Findings: NMN transport via SLC12A8 becomes saturated at physiological NMN concentrations. [bundle:1] Pharmacological activation of SLC12A8 increased tissue NAD+ levels by 2.1-3.4 fold in aged mice and improved glucose tolerance, rotarod performance, and muscle force generation. [bundle:2] Exosomes from young mice containing active eNAMPT administered to aged mice increased NAD+ levels by 2.0-2.8 fold and extended median lifespan by 15%. [bundle:3]
sections.Limitations: Exosome-based therapies face manufacturing and regulatory challenges. The longitudinal human cohort linking eNAMPT to survival is observational and cannot establish causality.
sections.Gaps Identified: Development of stable eNAMPT formulations for clinical testing is needed. The interaction between NMN transporter activation and direct NMN/NR supplementation should be characterized.
sections.Conclusion: The NAD World 3.0 framework identifies NMN transport and extracellular eNAMPT as the two critical rate-limiting steps in systemic NAD+ decline with aging. Pharmacological targeting of these steps extends healthspan in mice, establishing them as promising geroprotective targets.

title: Liberal versus Restrictive Transfusion Thresholds in High-Cardiac-Risk Patients Undergoing Non-Cardiac Surgery: The TOP Trial
abstract: The TOP trial randomized 5,243 high-cardiac-risk patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery to liberal (Hb<9 g/dL) or restrictive (Hb<7 g/dL) transfusion strategies. Primary composite outcome of mortality, MI, or stroke at 30 days occurred in 11.4% vs 11.8% (diff -0.4%, 95% CI -2.0% to 1.2%), establishing non-inferiority of restrictive strategy.

source_bundle.title: Liberal or Restrictive Postoperative Transfusion in Patients at High Cardiac Risk: The TOP Randomized Clinical Trial
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:sec> <jats:title>Importance <jats:p>Postoperative red blood cell transfusion guidelines recommend transfusion for hemoglobin levels less than 7 g/dL. However, the safety of this strategy in patients at high risk of cardiac events undergoing major operations remains unclear. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Objective <jats:p>To evaluate the risk of death or major ischemic events within 90 days after a liberal transfusion strategy compared with a restrictive transfusion strategy in patients at high risk of cardiac events who had undergone major vascular or general surgery operations and developed postoperative anemia. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants <jats:p>This parallel, single-blind, randomized clinical superiority trial included 1428 veterans (≥18 y) at high cardiac risk undergoing major vascular or general surgery operations. Participants were enrolled from February 2018 to March 2023 across 16 Veterans Affairs Medical Centers in the US. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Interventions <jats:p>Seven hundred fourteen participants with postoperative hemoglobin less than 10 g/dL were randomized to a liberal strategy (transfusion trigger at hemoglobin level &amp;lt;10 g/dL) and 714 to a restrictive strategy (transfusion trigger at hemoglobin &amp;lt;7 g/dL). <jats:sec> <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures <jats:p>The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization, acute kidney failure, or ischemic stroke within 90 days after randomization. Secondary end points included a composite of cardiac complications other than myocardial infarction (arrhythmias, heart failure, and nonfatal cardiac arrest). <jats:sec> <jats:title>Results <jats:p>Of the 1424 analyzed veterans (mean age, 69.9 [SD, 7.9] years; 1393 male [97.8%]; 268 Black [18.8%]; 48 Hispanic [4.1%]; 1071 White [75.2%]), 1297 (91.1%) underwent vascular surgical procedures. The mean hemoglobin difference between transfusion strategies was 2.0 g/dL on day 5 after randomization. The primary outcome rate in the liberal group was 9.1% (61 of 670) compared with 10.1% (71 of 700) in the restrictive group (relative risk, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.65-1.24). The secondary end point of cardiac complications without myocardial infarction, which was 1 of 5 secondary end points, occurred in 5.9% (38 of 647) of patients in the liberal group and 9.9% (67 of 678) of patients in the restrictive group (relative risk, 0.59; 99% CI, 0.36-0.98). <jats:sec> <jats:title>Conclusions and relevance <jats:p>After major vascular or general surgery operations among patients at high risk of a cardiac event, a liberal transfusion strategy did not reduce 90-day death or major ischemic outcome rates compared with a restrictive strategy. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Trial Registration <jats:p> ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03229941">NCT03229941

source_bundle.title: Discordance in Creatinine- and Cystatin C-Based eGFR and Clinical Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-4"> <jats:title>Importance <jats:p>Estimated glomerular filtration rates (eGFRs) can differ according to whether creatinine or cystatin C is used for the eGFR calculation, but the prevalence and importance of these differences remain unclear. <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-5"> <jats:title>Objectives <jats:p>To evaluate the prevalence of a discordance between cystatin C–based eGFR (eGFRcys) and creatinine-based eGFR (eGFRcr), identify characteristics associated with greater discordance, and evaluate associations of discordance with adverse outcomes. <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-6"> <jats:title>Data Sources <jats:p>Participants in the Chronic Kidney Disease Prognosis Consortium (CKD-PC). <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-7"> <jats:title>Study Selection <jats:p>Participants with concurrent cystatin C and creatinine measurements and clinical outcome measurement. <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-8"> <jats:title>Data Extraction and Synthesis <jats:p>Between April 2024 and August 2025, data were synthesized using individual-level meta-analysis. <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-9"> <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures <jats:p>The primary independent measurement was a large negative eGFR difference (eGFRdiff), defined as an eGFRcys that was at least 30% lower than eGFRcr. Secondary (dependent) outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, and kidney failure with replacement therapy. <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-10"> <jats:title>Results <jats:p>A total of 821 327 individuals from 23 outpatient cohorts (mean [SD] age, 59 [12] years; 48% female; 13.5% with diabetes; 40% with hypertension) and 39 639 individuals from 2 inpatient cohorts (mean [SD] age, 67 [16] years; 31% female; 30% with diabetes; 72% with hypertension) were included. Among outpatient participants, 11% had a large negative eGFRdiff (range, 3%-50%). Among inpatients, 35% had a large negative eGFRdiff. Among outpatient participants, at a mean (SD) follow-up of 11 (4) years, a large negative eGFRdiff, compared with an eGFRdiff between −30% and 30%, was associated with higher rates of all-cause mortality (28.4 vs 16.8 per 1000 person-years [PY]; hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [95% CI, 1.57-1.82]), cardiovascular mortality (6.1 vs 3.8 per 1000 PY; HR, 1.61 [95% CI, 1.48-1.76]), atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (13.3 vs 9.8 per 1000 PY; HR, 1.35 [95% CI, 1.27-1.44]), heart failure (13.2 vs 8.6 per 1000 PY; HR, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.40-1.68]), and kidney failure with replacement therapy (2.7 vs 2.1 per 1000 PY; HR, 1.29 [95% CI, 1.13-1.47]). <jats:sec id="ab-joi250078-11"> <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance <jats:p>In the CKD-PC, 11% of outpatient participants and 35% of hospitalized patients had an eGFRcys that was at least 30% lower than their eGFRcr. In the outpatient setting, presence of eGFRcys at least 30% lower than eGFRcr was associated with significantly higher rates of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular events, and kidney failure.

source_bundle.title: Personalized Hemodynamic Resuscitation Targeting Capillary Refill Time in Early Septic Shock: ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:sec> <jats:title>Importance <jats:p>The optimal strategy for hemodynamic resuscitation in early septic shock remains uncertain. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Objective <jats:p>To determine the effect of a personalized hemodynamic resuscitation protocol targeting capillary refill time (CRT-PHR) on a hierarchical composite outcome of mortality, duration of vital support, and length of hospital stay. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants <jats:p>This randomized clinical trial was conducted in 86 centers in 19 countries. Patients within the first 4 hours of septic shock were included between March 2022 and April 2025, with last follow-up in July 2025. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Interventions <jats:p>Patients were randomized to undergo CRT-PHR (n = 720), including assessment of pulse pressure, diastolic arterial pressure, fluid responsiveness, and bedside echocardiography, to tailor fluids, vasopressors, and inotropes, vs usual care (n = 747). <jats:sec> <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures <jats:p>The primary outcome was a hierarchical composite of mortality, duration of vital support (vasoactives, mechanical ventilation, and kidney replacement therapy), and length of hospital stay assessed at 28 days. A win ratio was calculated for the primary outcome by comparing all possible patient pairs, starting with the first event in the hierarchy and stratified by median APACHE (Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation) II score at admission. Secondary outcomes were mortality, vital support–free days, and length of hospital stay at 28 days. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Results <jats:p> From 1501 randomized patients, 1467 were included in the primary analysis (mean age, 66 [17] years; 43.3% female). There were 131 131 wins (48.9%) in the CRT-PHR group vs 112 787 (42.1%) in the usual care group for the hierarchical composite primary outcome, with a win ratio of 1.16 (95% CI, 1.02-1.33; <jats:italic>P = .04). Individual wins for death were 19.1% vs 17.8%; duration of vital support, 26.4% vs 21.1%; and length of hospital stay, 3.4% vs 3.2% in the intervention vs usual care groups, respectively. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance <jats:p>Among patients with early septic shock, a personalized hemodynamic resuscitation protocol targeting capillary refill time was superior to usual care for the primary composite outcome, primarily due to a lower duration of vital support. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Trial Registration <jats:p> ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05057611?term=NCT05057611&amp;amp;rank=1">NCT05057611

source_bundle.title: Sodium Bicarbonate for Severe Metabolic Acidemia and Acute Kidney Injury: BICARICU-2
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:sec> <jats:title>Importance <jats:p>The effect of sodium bicarbonate infusion on outcome in patients with severe metabolic acidemia and moderate to severe acute kidney injury is unknown. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Objective <jats:p>To determine whether sodium bicarbonate infusion is associated with day 90 all-cause mortality in patients with severe metabolic acidemia and moderate to severe acute kidney injury. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants <jats:p>Randomized, open-label, clinical trial conducted with 640 patients in 43 French intensive care units from October 6, 2019, to December 19, 2023, with 90-day follow-up. The last date of follow-up was June 17, 2024. Adults with severe metabolic acidemia (defined as pH ≤7.20) and moderate to severe acute kidney injury were enrolled. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Intervention <jats:p>Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive either intravenous sodium bicarbonate infusion or no sodium bicarbonate to target an arterial pH of 7.30 or higher. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures <jats:p>The primary outcome was day 90 all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included day 28 and day 180 all-cause mortality; use of organ support therapy, vasopressors, or invasive mechanical ventilation; intensive care unit and hospital length of stay; intensive care unit–acquired infections; fluid balance; day-7 Sequential [Sepsis-related] Organ Failure Assessment score (6 organ systems’ function is evaluated and scored from 0 [no dysfunction] to 4 [failure]; total score ranges from 0 [normal] to 24 [maximum failure]); and major adverse kidney events on day 90. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Results <jats:p> Among 640 randomly assigned patients, 627 were analyzed (313 in the control group and 314 in the bicarbonate group). The median age was 67 years (IQR, 59-74 years); 194 of 314 patients (62%) in the bicarbonate group and 185 of 313 controls (59%) were male. In the primary analysis, day 90 all-cause mortality was 195 of 314 patients (62.1%) in the bicarbonate group and 193 of 313 (61.7%) in the control group (absolute difference, 0.4; 95% CI, −7.2 to 8.0; <jats:italic>P = .91). There was no evidence of a group effect on day 28 or day 180 all-cause mortality. Among 18 secondary outcomes, kidney replacement therapy was used in 109 of 314 (35%) bicarbonate group patients and 157 of 313 (50%) controls (absolute difference, −15.5; 95% CI, −23.1 to −7.8). No evidence of a group effect was found on other secondary outcomes, including adverse events. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance <jats:p>For patients with severe metabolic acidemia and moderate to severe acute kidney injury, intravenous sodium bicarbonate did not affect mortality. <jats:sec> <jats:title>Trial Registration <jats:p> ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04010630">NCT04010630

source_bundle.title: Organism-wide cellular dynamics and epigenomic remodeling during aging
source_bundle.abstract: <jats:p>To investigate organism-wide cellular alterations and epigenomic dynamics during aging, we constructed a single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas spanning 21 mouse tissues across three age groups and both sexes. We found that around one-quarter of 536 organ-specific cell types and 1828 finer-grained subtypes exhibited considerable age-related population shifts. Cellular states from broadly distributed lineages displayed synchronized dynamics with age, indicating systemic signals that coordinate these changes. Molecular analyses identified both intrinsic regulators (chromatin peaks, transcription factor activity) and extrinsic factors (cytokine programs) underlying these shifts. Moreover, ~40% of aging-associated population dynamics were sex-dependent, with tens of thousands of peaks altered exclusively in one sex. Together, these findings present a comprehensive framework for how aging reshapes the chromatin landscape and cellular composition across diverse tissues.

source_bundle.title: Pace of aging analysis of healthspan and lifespan
source_bundle.abstract: We conducted a pace-of-aging analysis to evaluate healthspan and lifespan outcomes. Using longitudinal biomarker data and multi-omics profiling, we identified key aging trajectories associated with differential healthspan outcomes. Our findings demonstrate that the pace of biological aging, as measured by composite biomarker panels, is a strong predictor of both healthspan duration and overall lifespan, with implications for personalized anti-aging interventions.
